This is goal g-33a7a4ae, round 2 (fix round; round 1 was audit-only and already merged as docs/state/silent-failures.md; several fix batches already merged for other files). Read that doc's methodology section first (top of file) and the per-file section for tools/batch.mjs (search for '### tools/batch.mjs' - it lists exact line numbers and the catch form found there: try-catch-no-binding or dot-catch-arrow).

IMPORTANT - this file is sensitive (MONEY): it is the real Anthropic Batch API client (createBatchCollector) - it submits paid batches, polls their status, and cancels them. Two flagged catches are directly billing-relevant and need UNCONDITIONAL visibility (never stay fully silent, regardless of error code), because the file's own comment says it out loud: 'the remote batch is cancelled too, so it stops running (and billing) for nobody':
  - `cancelRemote`'s own fetch call (`try { await fetchImpl(.../cancel, ...) } catch {}`): if this fails, the LOCAL state is already marked canceled/ended, but the REMOTE batch may keep running and billing with nobody tracking it. Log every failure here, no narrowing - there is no 'expected benign' version of a failed cancel call.
  - the expiry-triggered `cancelRemote(b).catch(() => {})` backstop a few lines later: same reasoning, log every failure here too (this one only fires if something in cancelRemote itself throws outside its own internal try, which should be rare and is itself worth seeing).

One more catch deserves extra care: `try { text = await res.text() } catch {}` right after a successful batch-creation POST. If reading the response body fails here, `text` stays empty, `parseJson` returns null, and the code falls into the 'batch-create-invalid' rejection path - but the batch may have ALREADY been created on Anthropic's side, and because we never captured its `b.id`, it can never be tracked or cancelled later (an orphaned, invisible, still-billing batch). Log this failure unconditionally too, for the same reason - this is not a narrow-to-ENOENT situation, it is 'we may have just lost track of money'.

The remaining flagged catches (`emit`'s onEvent wrapper, `runBatch(b).catch(() => {})`'s outer backstop, the `onSent` callback wrapper, and the same-host URL-parse check) are ordinary best-effort fallbacks around caller-supplied callbacks or input parsing, not billing-critical themselves - treat those per the normal rules below.

For EACH flagged line in tools/batch.mjs only (do not touch any other file, do not touch anything beyond the flagged catch blocks, do not change what any function returns, do not change when a batch is marked ended/canceled, do not change the billing-relevant control flow itself - only add visibility):

1. Read the surrounding function to understand what the catch is actually guarding against and what happens today when it swallows silently.
2. For the three money-critical catches named above: add a real error binding and an unconditional `console.error('[tools/batch.mjs] <short context>:', error?.message ?? error)` - no error-code narrowing, log every failure.
3. For the other four catches: decide case (a) expected/benign (keep the swallow, narrow to a specific error code if one makes sense, log anything else) vs case (b) genuinely unexpected (log unconditionally) - use `console.error('[tools/batch.mjs] <short context>:', error?.message ?? error)` for any new logging, this file has no other logger convention.
4. If a catch binds no error variable, add a REAL binding and reference it in a console.error call per the rules above - do not just rename-and-ignore a binding.

Do not refactor anything beyond the flagged catch blocks. Do not reformat unrelated code (this file uses no-semicolon/compact style in places - match it exactly where you edit). Do not rename functions or change exports. Preserve every existing behavior path exactly except for the narrowing/visibility described above.

Your workspace does not include the test suite, so you cannot run it yourself - the orchestrator runs the real full suite against your output after integration, and will also get this reviewed via the claude CLI before merge given the sensitivity (money/paid-API), and will send back any issue as a follow-up. List, in your final summary, which of the 7 flagged lines you touched, how (unconditional money-critical log, case a, or case b), with one line each, and confirm no batch's created/canceled/ended state or billing-relevant control flow changed.
